- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

<function call omitted for brevity>

assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. 1 # Zimmermann: Figma-To-React Handover Workflow, Confirmatory Audit 2 3 > **Date:** 2026-07-20 4 > **Prepared By:** Marcel Angelo Navarro (Front-End Development Lead) 5 > **Subject:** The Zimmermann "DDP Design OS" repository, handed over by the design team as a Figma-To-React deliverable. 6 > **Nature:** Confirmatory and extended audit. It re-verifies the concerns already raised by both the engineering team and the design team, and continues the review into the workflow itself (the pipeline as designed), artifact provenance, and reproducibility toward a React build. 7 8 --- 9 10 ## 1. Executive summary 11 12 **The single most important conclusion: this repository is a well-documented library of vanilla Web Components plus static HTML viewers. It is not, today, a Figma-to-React handover, even though `react` is a declared target stack.** There is no build system, no React code, no token export, and the shipped components have structural traits that make them unsafe to drop into React unchanged. The four concerns raised at handover are all confirmed, and each traces to a specific, nameable gap in the workflow as designed, not to isolated mistakes. 13 14 **Root-cause chain (the "why" behind every symptom):** 15 16 1. The extraction workflow captures a **static, single-viewport pixel snapshot** and discards the Figma data that encodes responsive intent (auto-layout hug/fill/fixed, constraints, min/max, variable modes). Building partly from **screenshots** made this worse: a screenshot is a fixed-width raster with no layout metadata at all. Result: absolute px, desktop-first, no fluid rules. (Concerns #1 and #2.) 17 2. Every quality rule in the pipeline is **prose guidance, not an executable gate.** The only automated check, `validate.mjs`, verifies the atomic-model taxonomy and nothing else, yet is presented as the definition of done. `Ready for Build` is a self-declared answer to a prompt. So non-responsive, injection-prone, spec-less, unverified output passes unchallenged. 18 3. **React is a declared stack that the pipeline never services.** No skill emits a React component, a prop/event contract, or a Code Connect map; the contract models string attributes only. React integration is explicitly "out of scope." (Concern #4, engineering-stack side.) 19 4. **Figma is not required and is never verified.** Screenshots, PDFs, URLs, and written descriptions are accepted as first-class, equal-fidelity spec sources; the Figma MCP connection is never checked before an extraction claims to be "from Figma"; and the Figma PAT is not set, so nothing can be re-verified now. (Concern #4, provenance side.) 20 21 **Severity dashboard (distinct issues after de-duplication):** 22 23 | Severity | Count | Headliners | 24 |---|---|---| 25 | Critical | 6 | Token base traced to a Figma file named "MCP-Test--Don-t-Use"; no handover quality gate; React declared but never produced; form controls unusable in React; systemic HTML injection; nothing verifiable against Figma (PAT unset). | 26 | High | 12 | No responsive capture anywhere; fixed-px token layer; 12 of 27 components have no spec; doc-vs-impl token conflicts; keyboard-inoperable nav; extraction discards Figma constraints; screenshot-sourced specs unmarked. | 27 | Medium | ~14 | Shadow-DOM/global-CSS conflict and duplicated type layer; contract `composes` inaccuracies; no focus management; no reduced-motion; import.meta.url bundler breakage; broken prototype-to-spec links; no tests/lint/CI. | 28 | Low | ~10 | Foreign path in `settings.json`; em-dash convention violations; INDEX legend drift; ghost `product-card` references; undocumented `ia/` and `shared/`. | 29 30 **What can be trusted:** 8 of 27 components are backed by a real, openable Figma node (Banner, Disclaimer, Footer, LogoMasthead, Navigation, TextInput, CardEditorial, and Button with caveats). The token adoption discipline is genuinely good (783 `var()` references, only 2 stray hex in component code). Git hooks, `.gitignore`, and the static `vercel.json` are sound. The atomic-model taxonomy is internally consistent. 31 32 --- 33 34 ## 2. Root-cause analysis: the workflow as designed 35 36 The produced artifacts are downstream effects. The causes live in `.claude/skills/`. This section is the heart of the "workflow weak areas" question. 37 38 **2.1 No responsive capture instruction exists in the pipeline.** A repo-wide search of `.claude/skills/` returns zero occurrences of "mobile-first", "desktop-first", `clamp(`, or "fluid". Component extraction (`extract/library.md:150`) reads only "structure, variants, states, and style values"; it never reads Figma resize behaviour or constraints. The spec instruction `extract/specs.md:234-235` says literally "Record **exact values**", which directs the agent to freeze pixels. A "Responsive behaviour" section exists only in the template/page spec format (`extract/specs.md:295-296`); the component and screen formats have none. Fixed px and an accidental viewport direction are therefore the guaranteed defaults. 39 40 **2.2 The extractor discards Figma's responsive metadata.** Auto-layout hug/fill/fixed, constraints, min/max, and variable **modes** (Figma's native mechanism for responsive and theme value sets) are never captured. Light/dark is reconstructed by hand via `[data-theme]` (`_shared/authoring.md:60-64`) rather than read from modes. The very data a developer needs to build responsive components is thrown away at read time. 41 42 **2.3 The handover has no gate.** `/handover` (`handover/SKILL.md:42-53`) runs extractions, generates the index, and commits. No coverage or verification step sits between. `Build Status` is set by asking the designer a question and writing the answer verbatim (`handover/index-generator.md:230-237`); nothing is checked before "Ready for Build" can be chosen. Worse, the index generator is explicitly told "Do not scan `02-design/specs/components/`" (`index-generator.md:34`), so the 12 missing specs are structurally invisible to the readiness document. 43 44 **2.4 The only automated check certifies almost nothing.** `validate.mjs` (`:50-119`) asserts valid tiers, composition arithmetic against the `composes` array, and that `` tags in demos resolve to contract entries. It does not check that specs exist, that a component's JS matches its contract, a11y, responsiveness, token usage, hardcoded literals, or that anything builds. It exits `0` ("Atomic model valid") while 12 specs are missing, `button.js` is full of hardcoded px, and platform layers are empty. Yet `contract/README.md` and `_shared/authoring.md:120-125` present a passing run as the definition of done. 45 46 **2.5 React is unserviced.** `authoring.md:115` mandates "Custom Elements only. Do not use JSX, directives, decorators." The contract schema models `enum`/`boolean`/`string` **attributes** only, with no `properties` and no `events` (grep for `dispatchEvent`/`CustomEvent` in `extract/` and `_shared/`: 0 hits). `atomic-model.md:87` and `specs.md:317` both declare framework assembly "outside the scope." So React, the actual engineering target, receives nothing React-shaped. 47 48 **2.6 Figma is optional and unverified.** The `/extract` router (`extract/SKILL.md:46-54`) accepts images, PDFs, Storybook URLs, live sites, and written descriptions as first-class spec sources; none is tiered as lower-fidelity. No step confirms the Figma MCP is connected before claiming a Figma read. Screenshot-sourced specs get only a prose `[estimated]` note (`specs.md:127-129`) that dies in the spec body and never reaches the handover surface. 49 50 **2.7 Shadow DOM and global CSS are mandated together, unreconciled.** Every component uses `attachShadow` (`library.md:199,233`), while `authoring.md:51` and `index-generator.md:98` describe `common.css` as holding "component base styles" to be "referenced in all component CSS." Only CSS custom properties cross the shadow boundary; class and element base styles do not. So the "base styles" in `common.css` are unreachable by every component, forcing each to re-declare typography. This is the mechanism behind the "monolithic / duplicated styles" concern. 51 52 **2.8 Prohibitions without enforcement.** "Never hardcode a hex, pixel, or font value" (`authoring.md:53`, `library.md:232`) is agent guidance; the only check (`library.md:374-378`) merely asks "Convert any to named tokens?" and is skippable. It was skipped: `button.js` ships `padding: 8px`, `width: 20px`, `border-radius: 2px`, and more. 53 54 **2.9 Whole delivery stages have no owning skill:** React componentization, token-to-theme export, accessibility validation, and testing/visual-regression. The pipeline stops at markdown specs plus vanilla elements and hands the four hardest stages to the dev team with no artifact and no check. 55 56 --- 57 58 ## 3. Findings by theme 59 60 Severity: **CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW**. Each finding: evidence, impact, fix. 61 62 ### A. Provenance and source-of-truth fidelity 63 64 - **[CRITICAL] The token base layer traces to a Figma file named "MCP-Test--Don-t-Use", and two different files are cited as the source of truth.** The 2026-07-08 base extraction of all colours, type, and spacing cites `MCP-Test--Don-t-Use` (`common.css:2`; `tokens.md:6`, file key `IxUGRtXKPyqdMV7UVuqaiv`). The 2026-07-14 alias remap and every Figma-citing component spec instead cite `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` (`tokens.md:4`, key `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`). The primitive layer that every component inherits sits on a file whose name says "don't use," never reconciled to the real design-system file. Fix: confirm the authoritative file and re-derive the primitive tokens from it. 65 - **[CRITICAL] Nothing can be verified against Figma right now.** `CLAUDE.local.md:14` shows the Figma PAT is `not set`, and `.claude/mcp.json` configures only `markitdown` (no Figma MCP). So the 8 node ids cannot be opened, the 6 "Figma unavailable" reverse-derived specs cannot be re-pulled, and every "verify with design owner" flag in `tokens.md` is currently unactionable. 66 - **[HIGH] Documentation and implementation disagree on load-bearing token values.** `--zimm-size-action-gap` is `16px` in `common.css:247` but `0px` in `tokens.md:258` (consumed by the button). `--zimm-scale-1200` is `48px` in `common.css:226`, but `tokens.md:3,248` claim it was remapped to 64px; the remap was never applied to the CSS (a 33% difference on a token used by footer, navigation, and mega-menu). 67 - **[HIGH] Specs cite CSS variables that do not exist.** `footer.md:19-21` lists `--zimm-color-bg-inverse`, `--zimm-color-bg-inverse-deep`, `--zimm-color-text-inverse-muted` (0 occurrences in `common.css`; the code uses `--zimm-color-bg-05/06` and `--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey`). `navigation.md:651` cites `--zimm-color-bg-page` (0 occurrences; code uses `--zimm-color-bg-07`). A dev implementing from these specs references undefined tokens. 68 - **[MEDIUM] Unresolved colour conflict.** `tokens.md:74` documents inverse grey as `#939393`; `common.css:124` implements `#969696` and comments it "confirmed"; `footer.md:322` says the Figma value `#939393` differs and to "verify with design." Unresolved. 69 - **[MEDIUM] A motion easing appears lifted from a prohibited external reference.** `tokens.md:166-167` documents `out-soft: cubic-bezier(0.20,0,0,1)`, identical to Loewe's `ease-out-soft` (`01-context/summaries/loewe-apc-en-home.md:115`), which project rules explicitly forbid copying (`project-context.md:56`). Mitigant: all motion is flagged PLACEHOLDER (`common.css:249-253`). It also does not exist in the CSS (the CSS defines `slides`/`fades` instead, which are undocumented). 70 - **[LOW-MEDIUM] Weak artifact-level audit trail.** The contract (`zimm-contract.js`), the declared single source of truth, has no changelog block. Element JS files carry no provenance headers (only `text-input.js` has two inline Figma comments). Off-scale/inferred values are explicitly noted: grid margins `30/24/0` "no matching token" (`common.css:236`), border-width "inferred from component inspection" (`tokens.md:280`). 71 72 **Provenance totals: 8 of 27 have a real Figma node id; 10 of 27 have a screenshot asset; 8 of 27 have measurements confirmed against Figma; 16 of 27 are unverified or unverifiable; 12 of 27 have no spec at all.** Full matrix in section 4. 73 74 ### B. Responsiveness and the token layer (Concerns #1 and #2) 75 76 - **[HIGH] Zero fluid sizing anywhere.** No `clamp()`/`min()`/`max()` in any file. All five font sizes and their line-heights are fixed px (`common.css:178-189`); the entire spacing scale is fixed px (`:201-213`). Fixed-px line-heights weaken WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text) and 1.4.10 (Reflow). 77 - **[HIGH] The token system has no responsive primitives.** `tokens.md` itself records "Grid / Breakpoints: Not found" and "Z-index: Not found." No breakpoint tokens; grid margins hardcoded (`common.css:238-240`). The staticness is in the source of truth, so a React port inherits it. 78 - **[HIGH] Fixed-pixel layout dimensions that never reflow.** Prototype templates carry `height:1047px`, `column-gap:100px`, `--hero-width: calc(100% - 776px)`, `width:210px` (`product-listing/assets/styles.css:76,99,106,167`), repeated in `product-detail`. 2 of 3 page templates have no width breakpoints. 79 - **[HIGH, direction] Mixed, not mobile-first.** Component media queries: 15 `min-width` vs 12 `max-width`. Desktop-first (`max-width`) components: `product-showcase-blocks`, `navigation`, `card-editorial`, `logo-masthead`, `hero-blocks`, `card-baseline`. Mobile-first: `footer`, `disclaimer`, `banner`, and the `.zimm-grid` foundation. `navigation.js` mixes both directions. Three different "desktop" breakpoints are in use (1024, 1280, 1440). The complex layouts were authored at desktop with mobile retrofitted, the tell of a desktop-frame design process. 80 - **[MEDIUM] Token bypass where a token exists.** `width/height:20px` instead of `--zimm-icon-size-lg` (`button.js:48-49`); `1px` instead of `--zimm-border-width-default`; raw `200ms/300ms/0.15s/400ms` instead of motion tokens. 81 - **[LOW] `.zimm-text-serif` defined twice** with conflicting properties (`common.css:321-323` and `402-409`); 7 unnecessary `!important` in shadow DOM; z-index magic numbers (1/100/200) with no scale; smallest type token is 10px. 82 83 ### C. Styling architecture (Concern #3, corrected) 84 85 - **[MEDIUM, with correction] The "everything in common.css" framing is a partial misdiagnosis.** Component styles are already co-located per component (about 737 lines of CSS embedded across the 27 shadow-DOM `.js` files; 99 `font-family` and 111 `font-size` declarations live inside components). `common.css` holds font-face, the `:root` tokens (correctly centralized), 23 `.zimm-text-*` utility classes, and the grid. 86 - **[MEDIUM] The real problem is a duplicated type layer.** Components reference the `.zimm-text-*` classes 0 times, because shadow DOM cannot see global classes. The 23 utility classes are usable only in light DOM (demos, catalog, prototypes), so every component re-implements typography from the raw tokens. The type system effectively exists twice. 87 - **[LOW] Inconsistent shared-file loading.** Only 3 components (the product-detail family) `` `common.css` into their shadow root; the other 24 rely on custom-property inheritance. Arbitrary and undocumented. Guidance for a React target: keep tokens shared, translate each component's already-co-located CSS into a module, and collapse the global text classes into token-driven text primitives. 88 89 ### D. Component code: security, correctness, React-readiness 90 91 - **[CRITICAL] Systemic HTML/attribute injection.** Nearly every component interpolates attribute values into `innerHTML` unescaped, both text-position and attribute-breakout. Examples: `banner.js:82`, `text-input.js:277`, `select.js:32` (options from consumer JSON), `button.js:53-54`. Several `href` sinks accept `javascript:` (`disclaimer.js:103`, `card-baseline.js:155,164`, `page-toolbar.js:108`). Only `mega-menu.js:17` escapes anything. Not exploitable as-shipped (demos render controlled data), but these are the reference implementations, so the pattern must be closed before production. Fix: a shared `escapeHtml()` plus attribute-quote escaping, or DOM built via `createElement`/`textContent`; allowlist `href` protocols. 92 - **[CRITICAL] Form controls are unusable in forms and in React.** `text-input`, `select`, `search` render native controls inside shadow DOM and expose `name`, but none are form-associated (no `formAssociated`/`attachInternals`; no `value` getter/setter). The internal `input`/`change` listeners only toggle CSS classes and never re-dispatch (`text-input.js:302-305`, `select.js:161-163`, `search.js:137-145`); native `change` is `composed:false`, so a React `onChange` never fires and the host does not participate in `
` submit or `FormData`. This contradicts the contract's claim that "form submission is native browser behaviour" (`zimm-contract.js:241`). 93 - **[HIGH] `innerHTML` re-render on every attribute change wipes live state.** `attributeChangedCallback` calls `_render()` which resets `shadowRoot.innerHTML` (`text-input.js:16,47`). Any React prop change destroys the user's typed value, focus, and caret. Directly hostile to React's re-render model. 94 - **[HIGH] Navigation controls are not keyboard-operable (WCAG 2.1.1/4.1.2).** The desktop search trigger is a `
` with no keydown handler (`navigation.js:639`); the account/wishlist/bag/search icons are bare `` (a labelled ``), not focusable, not buttons (`:643-680`). 95 - **[MEDIUM] React <=18 boolean-attribute hazard.** All booleans read via `hasAttribute` (`button.js:63,68,69`). # Zimmermann: Figma-To-React Handover Workflow, Confirmatory Audit > **Date:** 2026-07-20 > **Prepared By:** Marcel Angelo Navarro (Front-End Development Lead) > **Subject:** The Zimmermann "DDP Design OS" repository, handed over by the design team as a Figma-To-React deliverable. > **Nature:** Confirmatory and extended audit. It re-verifies the concerns already raised by both the engineering team and the design team, and continues the review into the workflow itself (the pipeline as designed), artifact provenance, and reproducibility toward a React build. --- ## 1. Executive summary **The single most important conclusion: this repository is a well-documented library of vanilla Web Components plus static HTML viewers. It is not, today, a Figma-to-React handover, even though `react` is a declared target stack.** There is no build system, no React code, no token export, and the shipped components have structural traits that make them unsafe to drop into React unchanged. The four concerns raised at handover are all confirmed, and each traces to a specific, nameable gap in the workflow as designed, not to isolated mistakes. **Root-cause chain (the "why" behind every symptom):** 1. The extraction workflow captures a **static, single-viewport pixel snapshot** and discards the Figma data that encodes responsive intent (auto-layout hug/fill/fixed, constraints, min/max, variable modes). Building partly from **screenshots** made this worse: a screenshot is a fixed-width raster with no layout metadata at all. Result: absolute px, desktop-first, no fluid rules. (Concerns #1 and #2.) 2. Every quality rule in the pipeline is **prose guidance, not an executable gate.** The only automated check, `validate.mjs`, verifies the atomic-model taxonomy and nothing else, yet is presented as the definition of done. `Ready for Build` is a self-declared answer to a prompt. So non-responsive, injection-prone, spec-less, unverified output passes unchallenged. 3. **React is a declared stack that the pipeline never services.** No skill emits a React component, a prop/event contract, or a Code Connect map; the contract models string attributes only. React integration is explicitly "out of scope." (Concern #4, engineering-stack side.) 4. **Figma is not required and is never verified.** Screenshots, PDFs, URLs, and written descriptions are accepted as first-class, equal-fidelity spec sources; the Figma MCP connection is never checked before an extraction claims to be "from Figma"; and the Figma PAT is not set, so nothing can be re-verified now. (Concern #4, provenance side.) **Severity dashboard (distinct issues after de-duplication):** | Severity | Count | Headliners | |---|---|---| | Critical | 6 | Token base traced to a Figma file named "MCP-Test--Don-t-Use"; no handover quality gate; React declared but never produced; form controls unusable in React; systemic HTML injection; nothing verifiable against Figma (PAT unset). | | High | 12 | No responsive capture anywhere; fixed-px token layer; 12 of 27 components have no spec; doc-vs-impl token conflicts; keyboard-inoperable nav; extraction discards Figma constraints; screenshot-sourced specs unmarked. | | Medium | ~14 | Shadow-DOM/global-CSS conflict and duplicated type layer; contract `composes` inaccuracies; no focus management; no reduced-motion; import.meta.url bundler breakage; broken prototype-to-spec links; no tests/lint/CI. | | Low | ~10 | Foreign path in `settings.json`; em-dash convention violations; INDEX legend drift; ghost `product-card` references; undocumented `ia/` and `shared/`. | **What can be trusted:** 8 of 27 components are backed by a real, openable Figma node (Banner, Disclaimer, Footer, LogoMasthead, Navigation, TextInput, CardEditorial, and Button with caveats). The token adoption discipline is genuinely good (783 `var()` references, only 2 stray hex in component code). Git hooks, `.gitignore`, and the static `vercel.json` are sound. The atomic-model taxonomy is internally consistent. --- ## 2. Root-cause analysis: the workflow as designed The produced artifacts are downstream effects. The causes live in `.claude/skills/`. This section is the heart of the "workflow weak areas" question. **2.1 No responsive capture instruction exists in the pipeline.** A repo-wide search of `.claude/skills/` returns zero occurrences of "mobile-first", "desktop-first", `clamp(`, or "fluid". Component extraction (`extract/library.md:150`) reads only "structure, variants, states, and style values"; it never reads Figma resize behaviour or constraints. The spec instruction `extract/specs.md:234-235` says literally "Record **exact values**", which directs the agent to freeze pixels. A "Responsive behaviour" section exists only in the template/page spec format (`extract/specs.md:295-296`); the component and screen formats have none. Fixed px and an accidental viewport direction are therefore the guaranteed defaults. **2.2 The extractor discards Figma's responsive metadata.** Auto-layout hug/fill/fixed, constraints, min/max, and variable **modes** (Figma's native mechanism for responsive and theme value sets) are never captured. Light/dark is reconstructed by hand via `[data-theme]` (`_shared/authoring.md:60-64`) rather than read from modes. The very data a developer needs to build responsive components is thrown away at read time. **2.3 The handover has no gate.** `/handover` (`handover/SKILL.md:42-53`) runs extractions, generates the index, and commits. No coverage or verification step sits between. `Build Status` is set by asking the designer a question and writing the answer verbatim (`handover/index-generator.md:230-237`); nothing is checked before "Ready for Build" can be chosen. Worse, the index generator is explicitly told "Do not scan `02-design/specs/components/`" (`index-generator.md:34`), so the 12 missing specs are structurally invisible to the readiness document. **2.4 The only automated check certifies almost nothing.** `validate.mjs` (`:50-119`) asserts valid tiers, composition arithmetic against the `composes` array, and that `` tags in demos resolve to contract entries. It does not check that specs exist, that a component's JS matches its contract, a11y, responsiveness, token usage, hardcoded literals, or that anything builds. It exits `0` ("Atomic model valid") while 12 specs are missing, `button.js` is full of hardcoded px, and platform layers are empty. Yet `contract/README.md` and `_shared/authoring.md:120-125` present a passing run as the definition of done. **2.5 React is unserviced.** `authoring.md:115` mandates "Custom Elements only. Do not use JSX, directives, decorators." The contract schema models `enum`/`boolean`/`string` **attributes** only, with no `properties` and no `events` (grep for `dispatchEvent`/`CustomEvent` in `extract/` and `_shared/`: 0 hits). `atomic-model.md:87` and `specs.md:317` both declare framework assembly "outside the scope." So React, the actual engineering target, receives nothing React-shaped. **2.6 Figma is optional and unverified.** The `/extract` router (`extract/SKILL.md:46-54`) accepts images, PDFs, Storybook URLs, live sites, and written descriptions as first-class spec sources; none is tiered as lower-fidelity. No step confirms the Figma MCP is connected before claiming a Figma read. Screenshot-sourced specs get only a prose `[estimated]` note (`specs.md:127-129`) that dies in the spec body and never reaches the handover surface. **2.7 Shadow DOM and global CSS are mandated together, unreconciled.** Every component uses `attachShadow` (`library.md:199,233`), while `authoring.md:51` and `index-generator.md:98` describe `common.css` as holding "component base styles" to be "referenced in all component CSS." Only CSS custom properties cross the shadow boundary; class and element base styles do not. So the "base styles" in `common.css` are unreachable by every component, forcing each to re-declare typography. This is the mechanism behind the "monolithic / duplicated styles" concern. **2.8 Prohibitions without enforcement.** "Never hardcode a hex, pixel, or font value" (`authoring.md:53`, `library.md:232`) is agent guidance; the only check (`library.md:374-378`) merely asks "Convert any to named tokens?" and is skippable. It was skipped: `button.js` ships `padding: 8px`, `width: 20px`, `border-radius: 2px`, and more. **2.9 Whole delivery stages have no owning skill:** React componentization, token-to-theme export, accessibility validation, and testing/visual-regression. The pipeline stops at markdown specs plus vanilla elements and hands the four hardest stages to the dev team with no artifact and no check. --- ## 3. Findings by theme Severity: **CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW**. Each finding: evidence, impact, fix. ### A. Provenance and source-of-truth fidelity - **[CRITICAL] The token base layer traces to a Figma file named "MCP-Test--Don-t-Use", and two different files are cited as the source of truth.** The 2026-07-08 base extraction of all colours, type, and spacing cites `MCP-Test--Don-t-Use` (`common.css:2`; `tokens.md:6`, file key `IxUGRtXKPyqdMV7UVuqaiv`). The 2026-07-14 alias remap and every Figma-citing component spec instead cite `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` (`tokens.md:4`, key `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`). The primitive layer that every component inherits sits on a file whose name says "don't use," never reconciled to the real design-system file. Fix: confirm the authoritative file and re-derive the primitive tokens from it. - **[CRITICAL] Nothing can be verified against Figma right now.** `CLAUDE.local.md:14` shows the Figma PAT is `not set`, and `.claude/mcp.json` configures only `markitdown` (no Figma MCP). So the 8 node ids cannot be opened, the 6 "Figma unavailable" reverse-derived specs cannot be re-pulled, and every "verify with design owner" flag in `tokens.md` is currently unactionable. - **[HIGH] Documentation and implementation disagree on load-bearing token values.** `--zimm-size-action-gap` is `16px` in `common.css:247` but `0px` in `tokens.md:258` (consumed by the button). `--zimm-scale-1200` is `48px` in `common.css:226`, but `tokens.md:3,248` claim it was remapped to 64px; the remap was never applied to the CSS (a 33% difference on a token used by footer, navigation, and mega-menu). - **[HIGH] Specs cite CSS variables that do not exist.** `footer.md:19-21` lists `--zimm-color-bg-inverse`, `--zimm-color-bg-inverse-deep`, `--zimm-color-text-inverse-muted` (0 occurrences in `common.css`; the code uses `--zimm-color-bg-05/06` and `--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey`). `navigation.md:651` cites `--zimm-color-bg-page` (0 occurrences; code uses `--zimm-color-bg-07`). A dev implementing from these specs references undefined tokens. - **[MEDIUM] Unresolved colour conflict.** `tokens.md:74` documents inverse grey as `#939393`; `common.css:124` implements `#969696` and comments it "confirmed"; `footer.md:322` says the Figma value `#939393` differs and to "verify with design." Unresolved. - **[MEDIUM] A motion easing appears lifted from a prohibited external reference.** `tokens.md:166-167` documents `out-soft: cubic-bezier(0.20,0,0,1)`, identical to Loewe's `ease-out-soft` (`01-context/summaries/loewe-apc-en-home.md:115`), which project rules explicitly forbid copying (`project-context.md:56`). It also does not exist in the CSS (the CSS defines `slides`/`fades` instead, which are undocumented). - **[LOW-MEDIUM] Weak artifact-level audit trail.** The contract (`zimm-contract.js`), the declared single source of truth, has no changelog block.
